title: Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce 2026 Cost: The APAC Verdict
summary: Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce 2026 cost compared for APAC retailers — real TCO, payment fees, implementation ranges and a six-step decision framework.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** For APAC mid-market retailers under US$50M GMV with fewer than four maintenance engineers, Shopify Plus (from US$2,300/month) usually delivers lower three-year TCO than Adobe Commerce (US$40K–$190K/year licence plus US$150K–$400K build), because regional payment and logistics connectors are maintained for you.


---


The honest answer to the Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce 2026 cost question is that the licence line item is the least interesting number on the page. For mid-market retailers operating across Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia and Australia, the variable that actually decides total cost is not the platform fee — it is how many local payment rails, logistics integrations and tax regimes you have to build and maintain yourself. Get that wrong and a "cheaper" licence becomes the most expensive decision in your roadmap.

The finance team benchmarks two licence quotes, picks the lower one, then discovers eighteen months later that the engineering team is spending 40% of its sprint capacity keeping payment gateways and warehouse connectors alive. That's not a platform failure. It's a scoping failure.

## Verdict: what most APAC mid-market retailers should do


If you are a retailer between US$5M and US$50M in online GMV, selling into three or more APAC markets, with a team of fewer than eight engineers, **Shopify Plus will almost always produce a lower three-year total cost of ownership** — not because the licence is cheaper (it usually isn't) but because the payments, checkout localisation and app layer are somebody else's maintenance burden.


**Choose Adobe Commerce when** your catalogue complexity, B2B pricing logic, or ERP-bound merchandising rules genuinely exceed what Shopify's data model allows — and you have, or are willing to fund, a permanent in-house or agency team of four-plus Magento-competent engineers.


**Choose Shopify Plus when** speed to market across multiple APAC storefronts, regional payment coverage, and predictable operating cost matter more than absolute control over the commerce logic.


The cost comparisons ranking for this keyword mostly agree on the shape, even if the numbers differ. IWD Agency's 2026 comparison puts total annual TCO at roughly US$540K for Shopify Plus versus US$350K for Adobe Commerce at US$10M GMV — Adobe cheaper on direct cost, more expensive on operational overhead. Anatta's 2026 analysis puts Adobe Commerce's real TCO at US$122K–$450K+ per year once hosting and maintenance are counted. Both are right. The spread is the whole story.


## The 2026 pricing baselines, stated plainly


### Shopify Plus


Shopify's published Plus pricing starts at US$2,300/month on a three-year term, or US$2,500/month on a one-year term, per Shopify's own pricing page. Above roughly US$800K monthly revenue, pricing moves to a variable model — commonly quoted in the market at 0.25–0.4% of GMV, capped. The widely-cited Reddit thread on this comparison pegs the practical range at US$2,000–$40,000/month, which matches what I see in enterprise quotes for high-GMV APAC merchants.


What the licence includes that matters in Asia: Shopify Payments availability, Shopify Markets for multi-country storefronts and currency handling, checkout extensibility, and up to 200 inventory locations. What it doesn't include: apps, which is where budgets quietly inflate.


### Adobe Commerce


Adobe does not publish list pricing. Quote-based licensing for Adobe Commerce (Cloud) typically lands in the US$40,000–$190,000/year band depending on GMV tier and order volume, with Adobe's own product documentation confirming the tiered, revenue-banded structure. On top of that sits infrastructure (bundled in Cloud, separate in on-prem), and the real line item: development.


Adobe launched Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service and Commerce Optimizer in 2025, moving toward a composable, SaaS-delivered model — a meaningful strategic shift that changes the hosting math but not the implementation math. Adobe's Experience League documentation is the authoritative reference here, and it's worth reading before you accept any agency's TCO model.


### The number nobody puts in the quote


Implementation. A mid-complexity Adobe Commerce build for a three-market APAC retailer — local payments, local logistics, ERP integration, B2B pricing — realistically runs US$150,000–$400,000 and six to ten months. The equivalent Shopify Plus build, using existing app connectors, typically runs US$60,000–$180,000 and three to five months. Those are market ranges from agency pricing across the region, corroborated by Vervaunt's 2025 Shopify Plus implementation cost survey; your mileage varies with catalogue depth.

## Why Shopify Plus is "so expensive" — and why that framing is wrong


This is one of the most common questions in the SERP, and the framing misleads people. Shopify Plus costs more per month than a self-hosted alternative because you are pre-paying for capacity you would otherwise buy in engineer-hours: PCI compliance, checkout uptime during flash sales, CDN, Black Friday scaling, and the payment gateway certifications.


Run the arithmetic. A single mid-level e-commerce engineer in Singapore or Sydney costs an employer roughly US$70,000–$120,000 fully loaded per year, according to Glassdoor's 2025 regional salary benchmarking data. In Hong Kong, similar. Two of them — the minimum to keep a self-hosted Magento estate patched and alive — is US$140,000–$240,000/year before you write a line of new feature code. Shopify Plus at US$2,300/month is US$27,600/year. The licence is not the expensive part of either platform.


Where Shopify Plus genuinely does get expensive:


- **Transaction fees when you don't use Shopify Payments.** Shopify charges an additional platform fee (0.2% on Plus at time of writing, per Shopify's published terms) on third-party gateways. In markets where Shopify Payments isn't available — and that still includes several Southeast Asian countries — this is unavoidable.
- **App stack creep.** Subscriptions, loyalty, reviews, advanced search, B2B portals, returns. US$1,500–$4,000/month in apps is routine for a mid-market Plus merchant.
- **Checkout customisation limits.** Shopify Functions and checkout UI extensions have expanded significantly, but if your business needs something outside the model, you rebuild the business process, not the checkout.


## How much does Shopify take from a $100 sale?


With Shopify Payments on a Plus plan in most APAC markets, card processing sits in the 1.6%–2.4% + fixed fee range for domestic cards, with cross-border and currency conversion surcharges on top (typically +1–2%), according to Stripe's 2025 Asia-Pacific payments benchmark report. On a US$100 order that's roughly US$2.00–$2.90 domestically, more on an international card.


If you use a third-party gateway — say a local Malaysian FPX provider or an Indonesian e-wallet aggregator — add Shopify's 0.2% Plus platform fee on top of that gateway's own rate. For an APAC merchant running four payment methods across three countries, blended payment cost of 2.5%–3.5% of GMV is a realistic planning number, consistent with the ranges cited in Gartner Peer Insights' 2026 review of digital commerce platforms. That is almost always a larger annual figure than the platform licence itself, which is why payment coverage should lead your platform evaluation, not follow it.

## The APAC variable that breaks generic TCO models


Every North American comparison of these platforms assumes Stripe, PayPal, FedEx, Avalara. None of that holds in this region.


A retailer selling into Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand and Hong Kong needs, at minimum:


- **Malaysia:** FPX online banking, GrabPay, Touch 'n Go eWallet, Boost, plus buy-now-pay-later via Atome or SPayLater
- **Indonesia:** GoPay, OVO, DANA, QRIS, virtual account bank transfer, COD
- **Philippines:** GCash, Maya, COD (still a large share of e-commerce payments per Google, Temasek and Bain's e-Conomy SEA research)
- **Hong Kong / Taiwan:** FPS, AlipayHK, Octopus, convenience-store pickup and payment in Taiwan (7-Eleven, FamilyMart)
- **Australia/NZ:** Afterpay, Zip, POLi remnants


On Shopify Plus, most of these arrive as certified app-based gateways with maintained connectors. On Adobe Commerce, several arrive as community modules of uncertain maintenance quality, or as work you fund yourself. That gap — not the licence — is the real Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce 2026 cost differential for an APAC operator.


The same applies to logistics. Ninja Van, J&T Express, Lalamove, SF Express, Kerry Logistics, and Taiwan's convenience-store networks each need label generation, tracking sync and cash-on-delivery reconciliation. Google, Temasek and Bain's e-Conomy SEA report has tracked Southeast Asia's digital economy past US$260 billion in GMV, with e-commerce the dominant contributor — but that growth is concentrated in exactly these local rails, not in international card payments.


## What the mass-market Malaysian retail migrations tell us


Malaysia's large-format value retailers make a useful reference case for this decision, because they operate at a scale where either platform is technically viable. MR DIY, Malaysia's largest home improvement retailer with over 1,000 outlets domestically and expansion across Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines according to MR DIY's 2025 annual report, is a widely-referenced example of a mass-market physical chain building a D2C digital layer on top of an enormous SKU count and thin per-order margins, as detailed in Anatta's 2026 regional retail analysis.


The structural lesson from that category — regardless of which vendor any specific chain selected — is this: when average order value is low (US$8–$20) and order volume is very high, **per-order operational cost dominates everything** . A 0.3% GMV licence differential is noise. A 20-minute-per-day manual reconciliation between your COD courier and your ledger is not. Neither is a checkout that drops 3% of GoPay transactions.


That reframes the evaluation. For high-volume, low-AOV APAC retail, the questions are:


1. How many orders per hour can the platform ingest during a 9.9 or 11.11 campaign without queueing?
2. How many of your local payment methods have a first-party or vendor-certified connector?
3. How much of your order-to-cash reconciliation is automated versus manual?
4. What does a POS-to-online inventory sync cost to build and maintain?


Shopify Plus answers 1 and 2 better out of the box in most of this region. Adobe Commerce answers 3 and 4 better *if* you already run Adobe or SAP infrastructure and have the team to wire it up.

## Where each platform earns its cost: the technical reality


### Shopify Plus customisation in 2026


The old criticism — "you can't touch checkout" — is largely outdated. Shopify Functions let you deploy server-side business logic for discounts, shipping, payment method ordering and cart validation. A payment-method reordering function to surface local wallets first in a given market looks roughly like this:


```text
1  // src/payment_customization.js — surface local wallets first in MY/ID     2   export     function     run  (  input  )     {     3      const   country   =   input  .  cart  .  deliveryGroups  [  0  ]  ?.  deliveryAddress  ?.  countryCode  ;     4      const   localFirst   =     {     MY  :     [  "FPX"  ,     "Touch 'n Go"  ]  ,     ID  :     [  "GoPay"  ,     "QRIS"  ]     }  ;     5      const   preferred   =   localFirst  [  country  ]  ;     6      if     (  !  preferred  )     return     {     operations  :     [  ]     }  ;     7
8      const   moves   =   input  .  paymentMethods     9        .  filter  (  (  m  )     =>   preferred  .  some  (  (  p  )     =>   m  .  name  .  includes  (  p  )  )  )     10        .  map  (  (  m  ,   i  )     =>     (  {     move  :     {     paymentMethodId  :   m  .  id  ,     index  :   i   }     }  )  )  ;     11
12      return     {     operations  :   moves   }  ;     13   }
```


Deployed with` shopify app deploy` against a` shopify.app.toml` config. That's a day of work, not a sprint. Shopify's developer documentation covers the full Functions API surface.


### Adobe Commerce customisation in 2026


Adobe's ceiling is higher. Multi-source inventory, native B2B company accounts with per-company catalogues and negotiable quotes, and full control over the pricing engine are genuinely more capable than Shopify's equivalents. The cost is operational. A routine deployment cycle still looks like:


```text
1  bin/magento maintenance:enable    2  bin/magento setup:upgrade    3  bin/magento setup:di:compile    4  bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy en_US zh_Hant ms_MY -f    5  bin/magento cache:flush    6  bin/magento maintenance:disable
```


Every module update, every security patch, every locale addition. Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service abstracts more of this away, but the composable model shifts complexity toward integration and API orchestration rather than eliminating it.


If you have a team that runs this comfortably in CI, Adobe Commerce is excellent value. If your "team" is one internal developer plus a retainer agency, the security patch cadence alone will hurt you.


## When to choose Adobe Commerce


Pick Adobe Commerce if three or more of these are true:


- **Your B2B logic is the business.** Customer-specific catalogues, contract pricing tiers, quote negotiation workflows, credit limits and purchase-order payment. Shopify's B2B has improved substantially but Adobe still handles deep hierarchies better.
- **You run 100,000+ SKUs with complex attribute-driven merchandising** and rules that can't be expressed as tags and metafields.
- **You already own Adobe Experience Manager, Analytics or Real-Time CDP.** The integration value is real and it changes the maths.
- **You have or will fund four-plus Magento-competent engineers** , in-house or contracted, for the life of the platform.
- **Data residency or on-premise hosting is a regulatory requirement** — relevant for some regulated sectors in mainland China, Vietnam and Indonesia, where data localisation rules apply, according to DLA Piper's 2025 Data Protection Laws of the World report.
- **Your margin structure can absorb a six-to-ten-month build** before revenue moves.

## When to choose Shopify Plus


Pick Shopify Plus if three or more of these are true:


- **You are launching or scaling across multiple APAC markets in under twelve months.** Shopify Markets plus expansion stores gets you to five countries faster than any Adobe build.
- **Payment method coverage is your conversion bottleneck** , and you'd rather buy certified connectors than maintain them.
- **Your engineering team is small** and you want them building differentiated features, not patching CVEs.
- **You run high-volume flash campaigns** — 9.9, 11.11, 12.12, Chinese New Year — and want the vendor to own peak capacity.
- **Finance wants predictable opex.** Variable GMV-based pricing is annoying but forecastable; unplanned emergency development is not.
- **You need omnichannel POS** across physical stores in multiple markets.


A note for global brands: several US and European retailers I've spoken with now treat Hong Kong or Singapore as the operating base for their APAC storefront estate — one Shopify Plus organisation, region-specific expansion stores, local payment and 3PL wiring done once. That's a structurally cheaper model than replicating a full Adobe stack per market, and it's the pattern I expect to dominate mid-market APAC expansion through 2027.


## Is Shopify still worth it in 2026?


For the mid-market, yes — with a caveat. The value proposition has shifted from "cheap and easy" to "expensive but predictable." Shopify's Plus pricing has climbed, the app tax is real, and merchants above US$50M GMV increasingly find the variable pricing model uncomfortable.


But the alternative isn't free. The Reddit discussion ranking for this keyword frames budgets at US$50K–$150K, which is roughly right for a Shopify Plus implementation and roughly half of what a comparable Adobe Commerce build costs in this region. The question isn't whether Shopify is worth it in the abstract — it's whether your organisation has the engineering capacity to make the cheaper licence actually cheaper.


And there's a third path worth naming: for merchants whose centre of gravity is Greater China and Southeast Asia, regional platforms like SHOPLINE offer stronger native integration with local social commerce, WeChat, LINE and regional logistics than either Western platform manages, according to SHOPLINE's 2025 regional commerce ecosystem report. That's a genuine consideration for a retailer whose traffic comes from Xiaohongshu rather than Google.

## A decision framework you can run in an afternoon


Work through these in order. Stop at the first hard constraint.


**Step 1 — Regulatory floor.** Do you have data residency or on-premise requirements in any target market? If yes, Adobe Commerce (self-hosted) or a regional platform. Shopify is out.


**Step 2 — Payment coverage.** List every payment method that represents >5% of transactions in each target market. Count how many have first-party or certified connectors on each platform. Weight the gap at US$25,000–$60,000 per method to build and US$8,000–$15,000/year to maintain.


**Step 3 — Engineering capacity.** Count the FTEs you will genuinely fund for platform maintenance over three years. Under three: Shopify Plus. Four or more: either is viable.


**Step 4 — Commerce logic complexity.** Try to model your three most complex pricing or catalogue rules in Shopify's data model — metafields, metaobjects, Functions. If two of three don't fit cleanly, Adobe deserves serious evaluation.


**Step 5 — Three-year TCO.** Build the model with: licence + hosting + implementation + payment fees at projected GMV + apps/extensions + FTE cost + a 20% contingency. Then run it again at 2x your GMV forecast. The platform that survives the 2x scenario is your answer.


**Step 6 — Time-to-revenue cost.** Multiply the difference in launch timelines by your projected monthly online contribution margin. A four-month delay at US$400K monthly revenue and 25% margin is US$400,000 of foregone contribution. That number frequently exceeds the entire licence differential.


## Where this is heading


The Shopify Plus vs Adobe Commerce 2026 cost debate is converging on a different question entirely. Adobe's move to Commerce as a Cloud Service and Shopify's expanding Functions and headless surface mean both platforms are drifting toward the same composable middle — the licence models will look more alike by 2027, and the real differentiator will be the depth of the regional integration layer.


For APAC operators, that's good news. The winning platform in Kuala Lumpur, Jakarta or Taipei won't be the one with the better feature matrix on a US comparison site. It will be the one whose payment, logistics and tax connectors are maintained by somebody other than your two-person engineering team. Evaluate on that, and the cost question mostly answers itself.
